svg.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: How to read an IR spectrum
svg.desc: An infrared spectrum in percent transmittance plotted against wavenumber from 4000 on the left to 400 cm⁻¹ on the right. Coloured bands mark the regions for O–H and N–H stretches (3200 to 3600), C–H stretches either side of 3000, triple bonds (2100 to 2260), C=O stretches (1650 to 1800) and double bonds, and the fingerprint region below 1500. A broad O–H dip, C–H dips and a strong sharp C=O dip at about 1712 are labelled.
svg.text: Wavenumber (cm⁻¹): high on the left, low on the right
Illustrative spectrum, not a real compound. Dips point down in transmittance.
